newsitem.title: USA: ASA Holdings sees Q2 below estimates.
newsitem.headline: ASA Holdings sees Q2 below estimates.

text.p: ASA Holdings Inc said on Thursday that its second quarter results will be below analysts' earnings estimates, because the the company is recording charges for the return of an aircraft and stock appreciation rights.
In a plan to standardize its fleet with Bombardier's CRJ aircraft, it is returning five BAe 146-200 aircraft to Jet Acceptance Corp, leading to a $2.6 million charge for return expenses, ASA said.

ASA also expects to incur a second quarter charge of $3.1 million associated with the finalization of its Stock Appreciation Rights program and adoption of a stock option plan that became effective May 21, 1997, the company said.
Analysts had expected ASA to earn $0.62 a share, according to First Call's consensus of earnings estimates. In last year's second quarter the company earned $0.59 a share.
The airline anticipates that the return of the BAe 146 will reduce its projected ASM growth during 1998 from 26 percent to 13 percent, it said.
However, the company expects that the rationalization of its fleet and the operating efficiencies of the CRJ will support analysts' estimates for 1998, ASA said.
